modes.label: per la famiglia Daví
modes.dedication: For the Daví family — the English original.
modes.summary: Three weeks and change: London, then Paris, where three men took an unrequested interest in our tickets at Gare du Nord and the city got roughly two hours of us before the 19:00 to Lyon. Lyon: champagne on the funicular hill, a cellar at fourteen degrees, bottles involved by the exit. Nice: one of the last berths on a small white ship — Claire booked it on the Monday under that day's one rule; I was informed on the Tuesday; we boarded Wednesday. Cabin 306, ten nights. Lipari, where I spent a serious minute assessing a 2003 Bordeaux that turned out to be the pepper grinder; the table has not let it go. Etna, with a driver who told us the eruption had finished and talked himself out of his own premium. Stromboli from the rail, free, the captain's idea. Valletta, Caravaggio — no joke there. And now the actual destination: Tuesday, Palermo, your table — the one introduction on this trip that cannot be improved on. Lunch is included; no appeals. Conditions remain grim. — Michael & Claire
modes.long:
*For the Daví family of Palermo. The Italian version reached you first; this is the original, sent so you can see how much the translation improved it.*

**Who arrives at your door.** Michael Kennedy, an accountant from Brisbane who has spent three weeks and change being corrected by professionals from London to Valletta, and Claire, who governs the expedition under a single law — one rule per day, hers, always right by evening. In Paris a man with a lanyard kindly inspected tickets nobody had asked him to inspect; the tickets survived. Paris itself received roughly two hours of us — in at 16:49, out on the 19:00 to Lyon — and the French state received my account of the lanyard with the warmth of a toll booth. We have been improving steadily since.

**Lyon.** Champagne on the funicular hill, a cellar at fourteen degrees, bottles involved by the exit. Somewhere that day Mont Blanc came off the plan — deferred.

**Nice.** One of the last berths on a small white ship: Claire booked it on the Monday under that day's one rule; I was informed on the Tuesday; we boarded on the Wednesday. Cabin 306, Deck 3, the water sitting in the joinery like part of the fittings. 184 passengers, 118 crew: the correct ratio for two people who had already demonstrated they could not be left unattended in a European railway station.

**Lipari — Filippino, est. 1910.** At Thursday lunch I gave a full, serious minute to what I took for a 2003 Bordeaux — colour against the light, a slow turn of the label, real professional gravity — before discovering it was the pepper grinder. Nobody at the table has let this go. I am telling you now so that you hear it from me first.

✻ If a pepper grinder is present on Tuesday, I am prepared to do it again.

**Lipari — the port.** Marina, red t-shirt, a one-woman taxi operation, opened at fifty. I negotiated her to forty-five with a photo stop thrown in, a result I remain proud of. By lunchtime she had forgotten me entirely.

**Etna.** The driver we messaged wrote back, unprompted, that the eruption had finished days ago — a man talking himself out of his own premium. We hired him on the spot: €450 for a volcano that had stopped, the phone calls included. Villagrande was full. Murgo was full. His friend made two calls down a chain and a door opened in Milo — Cantine Iuppa, one table deeper than the ones that were full — with a sommelier vouched in by name. There is no website for that. There will never be a website for that.

**At sea.** At dinner I asked one question about Stromboli, mostly to seem informed. That night the captain took her forty miles north and showed us Stromboli from the rail, doing what it does, for nothing. The best decision of the trip was made by somebody else, which by that stage surprised no one aboard.

**Valletta.** In the Co-Cathedral hangs the only canvas Caravaggio ever signed, and the signature is in the blood. We stood in front of it for a long time. I have no joke about it.

Here is what the winery taught us, and the captain, and Marina: the best of these islands cannot be booked. It can only be introduced — two phone calls, a name vouched in, a door that was never advertised opening anyway. Which brings us to Tuesday, because Aurora is the introduction. Your island keeps a saying for the children who go — *cu nesci arrinesci* — and it keeps it in Sicilian, not Italian, because the older language holds it better: who leaves, succeeds.

✻ Aurora — this line is yours to deliver.

Aurora left, and on the far side of the world our son Fraser — who keeps a notebook, rates everything, and does not spend his trust lightly — spends it on her without hesitation. That is the succeeding. But the proverb has a quiet second half that nobody writes down: the leaving points home. On Tuesday it points at your table, and we get to be sitting there when it lands.

**The road ahead.** Tuesday: lunch, Palermo, yours. Thursday: BA619 to London at noon, QF2 that evening as far as Sydney, and Brisbane on the Saturday morning, where the pepper-grinder story will be re-enacted on demand for years. One matter we settle now, in writing, where it cannot be reopened: aboard the ship, every good thing carries one word — *included* — and no appeal is heard against it. Tuesday's lunch sails under the same flag. The boat accepts no appeals, and neither do we. Everything else — the menu, the order of things, the length of the afternoon, whether the guests have eaten enough (they have not) — belongs to the Cruise Director alone.

Claire has already issued Tuesday's rule: arrive hungry, argue about nothing. We are complying with one of them.

Conditions remain grim.

— Michael & Claire Kennedy, Palermo, the night before

glossary.def: Meaning: everything is wonderful. To be delivered without smiling; a smile voids the sentence.
See above. Reserved for occasions when conditions have improved further.
Already paid for, therefore attending. The most beautiful word in the maritime language. No appeals are heard.
Better than done, when done would be worse. We did not see Mont Blanc; we deferred it. It is now perfect.
Claire's daily law. Exactly one per day, non-negotiable, and correct by evening without exception.
The two most powerful words in Italy, and our position for Tuesday: you decide. All of it.

modes.programme:
LE DUMONT D'URVILLE — PROGRAMME DU JOUR
Tuesday 1 September — Palermo. Ashore, in the best of hands.

12:30 — Guests delivered to the Daví table. Punctuality: we will do our best.
13:00 — Lunch commences. Duration: at the Cruise Director's discretion.
Dress: whatever la Signora approves of.
The bill: included. The boat accepts no appeals, and neither do we.
All remaining decisions: faccia lei.

✻ The Cruise Director may amend this programme at any hour, without notice, and will be right.

Cruise Director: la Signora Daví. Her word is final.

modes.label: for the six of you
modes.dedication: Nicholas · Sarah · Emily · Bryce · Lachlan · Fraser
modes.summary: Before the belt on Saturday, the short version. Three weeks and change: London, then roughly two hours of Paris, where we missed the 17:56 to Lyon by one minute — the rest is paperwork. Lyon: champagne up a hill on a funicular called the string, then the coolest cellar in France — fourteen degrees. Nice, then ten nights on a small ship — cabin 306, 184 passengers, 118 crew. Lipari, where your father spent a serious minute on what he believed was a 2003 Bordeaux. I'll explain at the belt. Stromboli, which the captain drove forty miles off her route to show us, for nothing. Malta, one painting worth the whole island. Sicily: a driver who told us the eruption had finished and talked himself out of his own premium, and a Tuesday lunch in Palermo that cannot be improved on. Then BA619, QF2, Sydney, Brisbane, Saturday morning, you six. Longer version below. Ratings table included, Fraser. Conditions remain grim. — Dad
modes.long:
For Nicholas, Sarah, Emily, Bryce, Lachlan and Fraser — to be read aloud before Saturday, in age order or by whoever seizes it first.

Your mother and I have been away three weeks and change, and I want the record straight before the arrivals belt, because your mother's version will be accurate and mine deserves a head start. Who arrives Saturday: a woman who was right about everything, on schedule, the whole way — and a man who over the same three weeks was beaten by a pepper grinder, a French timetable, and the honesty of a taxi driver. I'll take questions at breakfast.

**Paris.** Roughly two hours of it — in at 16:49, out on the 19:00, having missed the 17:56 to Lyon by one minute. There was some minor administration in between — handled, filed with the French state online that same night, four attachments, received with the warmth of a toll booth.

**Lyon.** The locals haul their city uphill on a funicular called la ficelle — the string — and have done since 1862, which Fraser will recognise as serious uptime. ✻ pause here; Fraser will want to verify the 1862. At the top, champagne at sunset, consumed under protest. Next day, Guigal's cellar: fourteen degrees, the coolest room in France that week. We went quiet in it. Bottles were involved by the exit; I have signed nothing stating how many. Somewhere that day Mont Blanc came off the plan — deferred.

**Lipari.** At Filippino — est. 1910 — lunch on the Thursday: your father spent a serious minute assessing what he believed was a 2003 Bordeaux — nose, label, gravity of expression, the lot — before discovering it was the pepper grinder. Your mother has not let it go. You are under no obligation to either. ✻ someone fetch the grinder from the kitchen before reading on; it helps. Also Lipari: a taxi driver named Marina, red t-shirt, one-woman operation, opened at fifty, and I negotiated her down to forty-five with a photo stop thrown in. I remain proud of this. She had forgotten it by lunch. Sarah — the granita is a 9.1 and I will defend that number at the belt.

**Etna.** The driver messaged before we'd even booked to say the eruption had finished days ago — talked himself out of his own premium. So we hired him on the spot, obviously: €450 for a volcano that had stopped, phone calls thrown in. Villagrande and Murgo were full; two calls down a chain and a door opened at Iuppa in Milo — one table deeper than the ones that were full, the sommelier vouched in by name. Nicholas — you know the three seconds after the tackle. Watch Sicilian traffic and work out what the horn actually is. Best defensive shape I've seen since your last game.

**At sea.** At dinner I asked one question about Stromboli, mostly to seem informed. That night the captain drove the ship forty miles north and showed us Stromboli from the rail, for free. The best decision of the trip was made by somebody else. This is the pattern. I've stopped fighting it.

**Valletta.** There is a painting there — Caravaggio's, the only one he ever signed, and he signed it in the blood. We stood in front of it a long time. I have no joke about it and I'm not inventing one. Emily — this is the one thing on the trip I'm not joking about; hold me to it Saturday.

**Palermo.** Tuesday's lunch was arranged by someone who knows the city better than the guidebooks admit, which is why it cannot be improved on.

Lachlan — I was beaten this trip by a pepper grinder, a timetable, and an honest taxi driver. Your mother was beaten by nothing. Draw no conclusions aloud. Bryce — run this through the checker. It will read as human, which is the nicest thing anyone has said about me all month.

Fraser — verified figures for the notebook. Methodology available on request. ✻ the table is Fraser's to read aloud; nobody else has the authority.

| Item | Rating |
|---|---|
| Granita | 9.1 |
| La ficelle (in service since 1862) | 8.8 |
| Pepper grinder, as wine | 2.0 |
| Pepper grinder, as pepper | 9.0 |
| Warmth of the French state | 1.5 |

Here is what I actually worked out, and I'll keep it short. We crossed from London to Sicily on a small, good ship — cabin 306, the water part of the joinery, 184 passengers, 118 crew — and every leg of it pointed the same direction: the arrivals belt in Brisbane on Saturday morning, where the six of you will be standing. That was the destination the whole time. Everything else was the string hauling us uphill towards it.

The road home: BA619 out of Palermo Thursday noon, QF2 out of London that evening, Sydney, then Brisbane, Saturday morning. Your mother arrives undefeated. I have a grinder to answer for.

Conditions remain grim.

— Dad

glossary.def: Everything is wonderful. To be delivered without smiling; smiling voids it.
Already paid for, and therefore we are attending. Ends all debate about whether anyone feels like it.
The plan. Not an itinerary — an itinerary can fail; the doctrine merely adapts.
Better than done, when done would have been worse. See: Mont Blanc, which is still there.
Italian for 'you decide' — the two most powerful words in Italy. Deploy on your mother at your own risk.
Your mother's daily law. There is only ever one. It is always right.

modes.label: for Mum & the tribe
modes.dedication: For Mum, and the siblings, in lieu of the postcard I forgot.
modes.summary: Three weeks and change. London first, Paris for roughly two hours (long story, no harm done), then Lyon, Nice, and ten nights on a small French ship — 184 passengers, 118 crew, our cabin low enough that the water sat in the window like part of the furniture. Down past a working volcano the captain detoured forty miles to show us for free, then Malta, then across to Sicily. Everyone is fed, rested, and sunburnt only in moderation. One report from the field: at lunch in Lipari I spent a serious minute assessing a 2003 Bordeaux before discovering it was the pepper grinder. Claire has photographs and intends to distribute them. Palermo Tuesday for a lunch we have been instructed to attend hungry, BA619 out of Palermo Thursday noon, QF2 that evening to Sydney, Brisbane Saturday morning. Roast on Sunday — programme attached. Conditions remain grim.
modes.long:
For Mum — who has always held that a thank-you doesn't count unless it's written down — and for the rest of you, who are copied in on principle.

The man coming home is the one you remember: overprepared, outnegotiated everywhere negotiation was offered, and now in possession of several hundred photographs of doorways. Claire, by contrast, ran the entire operation on one rule a day and has not lost an exchange since St Pancras. What follows is the honest record.

**Paris, for about two hours.** A man with a lanyard at Gare du Nord claimed to work for the métro; he did not, and it cost us nothing but minutes — we arrived at 16:49 and the 19:00 to Lyon left with us on it. I lodged a formal complaint with the French state that same evening, four attachments, and was received with all the warmth of a toll booth. The 19:00 was lovely.

**Lyon.** The locals call their funicular la ficelle — the string — and it has been hauling the city uphill since 1862. It hauled us up to the terraces at sunset, where champagne was consumed under protest. The next day Guigal's cellar, at fourteen degrees, was the coolest room in France that week. We went quiet in it the way you do in churches, and bottles were somehow involved by the exit. Somewhere that day Mont Blanc came off the plan — deferred.

**The ship.** Claire booked it on the Monday under that day's one rule; I was informed on the Tuesday; we boarded on the Wednesday — one of the last berths going. 184 passengers, 118 crew, which is a ratio Mum would approve of. Cabin 306, Deck 3, the water part of the joinery. Ten nights of somebody else doing the driving.

**Lipari.** At Filippino, which has been feeding people since 1910, at Thursday lunch, I gave what I firmly believed was a 2003 Bordeaux a long professional assessment — the label, the shoulder, the heft — before discovering it was the pepper grinder. The table has not let it go and shows no sign of starting.

✻ ask Claire for the photograph; the caption is doing heavy lifting.

Afterwards a taxi driver named Marina, red t-shirt, one-woman operation, opened at fifty and let me talk her down to forty-five with a photo stop thrown in. I was proud of that for most of a day. She had forgotten me by lunch.

**Etna.** Our volcano driver messaged ahead to say the eruption had finished days earlier and talked himself out of his own premium. We hired him on the spot. The mountain had stopped; the honesty hadn't. His friend then made two phone calls — Villagrande was full, Murgo was full — and the second call produced a sommelier vouched in by name and a table at Iuppa in Milo, one table deeper than the ones that were full. I have contributed nothing to this trip that two Sicilian phone calls couldn't beat.

**Stromboli.That night the captain, unasked, drove her ship forty miles north and showed us Stromboli doing its work from the rail, for free.

**Valletta.** Caravaggio signed one painting in his whole life. It hangs here, and the signature is in the blood. We stood in front of it for a long time, and I don't have a joke about it.

✻ pause after this one; it is read slowly or not at all.

Somewhere around Malta I noticed that every good thing on this crossing was handed to us by someone else, and lined up they all point the same direction: a table in Brisbane with all of you around it.

The road from here: Malta today — a wooden dgħajsa across the harbour, Mdina once the crowds thin, a silence worth the whole island. Palermo Tuesday — lunch has been arranged by someone who knows the city better than the guidebooks admit, which is why it cannot be improved on; we will attend hungry, as instructed. Then BA619 out of Palermo Thursday noon, QF2 out of London that evening, Sydney, and Brisbane on Saturday morning. Sunday is accounted for below.

Conditions remain grim.

glossary.def: Translation: everything is wonderful. To be delivered flat, without smiling. Smiling voids it.
Not cancelled — better than done, where done would have been worse. Mont Blanc is deferred. Follow-up questions are not taken.
Already paid for, and therefore attended. Aboard ship this covered the champagne; at home it covers the roast, in both directions.
Claire's daily law: each day is permitted exactly one non-negotiable, declared at breakfast. Undefeated since St Pancras. Household adoption recommended.
Italian: 'you decide' — the two most powerful words in Italy. Hereby transferred to Mum for domestic use, effective the first Sunday.

modes.programme:
LE DUMONT D'URVILLE — PROGRAMME DU JOUR
Sunday 6 September — Brisbane. Weather: superb, as arranged.

12:30 — Embarkation, the family dining room. Punctuality is a courtesy owed to the roast.
13:00 — Gala luncheon. Included.
14:15 — Enrichment lecture: "Three Weeks and Change, in Four Hundred Photographs," M. Kennedy. Questions permitted; mercy is not.
15:30 — Tea, and the formal hearing of the pepper-grinder matter.
✻ Claire chairs the hearing; the exhibits are already printed.

Dress: Sunday. Aprons by invitation only.
Cruise Director: Mum. Her word is final. The vessel accepts no appeals.

modes.label: for the mates
modes.dedication: For the group chat, which was kept deliberately under-informed.
modes.summary: Three weeks and change, London to Brisbane the long way. Paris: three men ran the oldest trick at Gare du Nord, got nothing, and the 17:56 to Lyon left one minute before we reached it — which was the actual robbery. Two hours in Paris, all told. Lyon, then Nice, then the ship Claire booked on the Monday under that day's one rule — I was informed on the Tuesday — one of the last berths, 184 passengers, 118 crew, cabin 306 with the water in the joinery, $23,280 since you'd ask. Lipari, where I gave a 2003 Bordeaux a serious minute of assessment at Thursday lunch before establishing it was the pepper grinder.Etna with a driver who told us the eruption had finished and talked himself out of his own premium — €450, hired on the spot. Malta. Palermo. BA619 Thursday noon, QF2 that night; Saturday morning, the belt. Full debrief at the pub; first round sorts the chair. Conditions remain grim.
modes.long:
*For the group chat, which was kept deliberately under-informed for three weeks and change and is now owed a full disclosure document.*

Consider this the interim market wrap. Three weeks and change, London to Brisbane the long way round. Positions were opened, positions were closed, and one asset could not be booked — only introduced. What arrives at the pub is a man who was out-traded by, in order: three pickpockets, a taxi driver in a red t-shirt, an Etna guide, a ship's captain, and a pepper grinder. Receipts follow.

**Gare du Nord.** A man wearing a lanyard announced he worked for the métro. He did not work for the métro. Two colleagues stood behind him with the posture of men who also did not. The tickets survived, the crew left for easier company, and the 17:56 to Lyon departed one minute before we reached it — which was the actual robbery. Two hours in Paris, all told: in at 16:49, out on the 19:00. I filed with the French state online that night, four attachments, and was received with the warmth of a toll booth. Net position: tickets retained, dignity marked to market, replacement TGV €148. Somewhere in those two hours Mont Blanc came off the plan — deferred.

**Nice.** Claire booked the ship on the Monday under that day's one rule; I was informed on the Tuesday; we boarded Wednesday — one of the last berths on her. 184 passengers, 118 crew, a staffing ratio no business any of us has ever run would survive a quarter of. Cabin 306, Deck 3, the water part of the joinery. $23,280, since you were going to ask before I'd sat down.

**Lipari — Filippino, est. 1910.** Thursday lunch. I gave a 2003 Bordeaux the full workup — label, colour, a serious minute of professional consideration — before establishing that it was the pepper grinder. A hundred and sixteen years that restaurant has been open; I doubt they've had a better Thursday. I put it on the record here only so that when it reaches you through Claire it can't be exaggerated. It doesn't need to be.

✻ pause after "pepper grinder"; the room will need it.

**Lipari, kerbside.** Marina — red t-shirt, one-woman operation — opened at fifty for the island loop. I closed her at forty-five with the photo stop thrown in. By lunch she had forgotten me entirely. Five euros. Any of you would have paid the fifty and been right.

**Etna.** The driver messaged before we'd even hired him to say the eruption had finished days earlier — talking himself out of his own premium. Hired on the spot. €450 for a volcano that had stopped, phone calls thrown in: Villagrande full, Murgo full, and then Cantine Iuppa in Milo — one table deeper than the ones that were full, the sommelier vouched in by name down a chain of two calls. I have paid more at home for considerably less, and so have you.

**The trade of the trip.** At dinner I asked one question about Stromboli, mostly to seem informed. That night the captain took her forty miles north, off her own route, and showed us Stromboli from the rail — going about its business, for free.The best decision of the trip was made by somebody else, which you will all agree is consistent with the fund's long-term record.

**The ledger.** Eurostar £981. Replacement TGV €148. Hotel Suisse $880. The ship $23,280. The 1926 $450. Marina €45. Etna €450. No totals row. Some numbers shouldn't be added up in front of witnesses.

✻ first round settles who reads the ledger aloud.

Somewhere between Malta and Sicily it occurred to me that none of this is actually banked until it's been told to people who will refuse to be impressed by any of it. A trip doesn't settle on the day; it settles at a table with the four or five people qualified to laugh at the pepper grinder properly. The pub is the clearing house. You lot are the settlement date. Palermo on the Tuesday, meanwhile, produced a lunch arranged by someone who knows the city better than the guidebooks admit, which is why it cannot be improved on.

**The road home.** BA619 out of Palermo, Thursday noon. QF2 out of London that evening, as far as Sydney; the last hop is a connector, and Saturday morning is the belt. Mont Blanc stays on the books as deferred, not cancelled — "I won't watch cams… Oppenheimer in 70mm" — so there is exactly one open position carried forward, and you'll hear about it when it closes.

First round sorts the chair.

Conditions remain grim.

The hardship continues.

glossary.def: Translation: everything is wonderful. To be delivered in a flat voice while holding a full glass. Smiling voids the warranty.
See above. Deployed when the first round lands. The two may be stacked for emphasis at close of business.
Already paid for, therefore attending. Ends all discussion of whether we're going. Applies equally to shore excursions and pub debriefs.
Better than done, when done would be worse. Not the same as cancelled, and anyone who says otherwise buys the next round.
'You decide' — the two most powerful words in Italy. Works on sommeliers, taxi drivers and, on the evidence of three weeks, me.
Claire's daily law: one thing per day done properly, everything else is a bonus. It works, I can't explain why, and I'm not taking questions on it.

modes.programme:
LE DUMONT D'URVILLE — PROGRAMME DU JOUR

Port of call: Brisbane. Berth: the usual pub.
Tender service: the Raptor.
18:00 — Embarkation at the bar. No boarding pass required; thirst will be verified.
18:05 — Welcome round. Included.
18:20 — Lecture: "Three Weeks and Change, Comprehensively Out-Traded" (M. Kennedy, no slides).
19:00 — Q&A. The pepper grinder question will be taken first, to get it over with.
19:30 — The ledger, read aloud. [NAME] is not to be given the calculator.

modes.label: for the two of us
modes.dedication: For us — the one room with no audience.
modes.summary: Three weeks and change, and this is the version with no audience in it. London did what London does. Paris took one minute off us and gave back a night in Lyon nobody had planned — you were behind me the whole time at the barriers, which is the fact I kept. The coast road asked nothing of us and we paid it in full. Then you found the last berth on a ship we had no business boarding and booked it before the sensible objections could assemble — the best decision of the fortnight, made inside a day, by you. A porthole with the whole Tyrrhenian in it. Malta was champagne on a balcony and a lift we rode for no reason either of us has offered. Tomorrow, Sicily; Tuesday, a table in Palermo where the answer to everything is faccia lei; Thursday, the long way home, upstairs. Conditions, between us, have never been grimmer.
modes.long:
*For us. Not for forwarding. The other four rooms got the stories; this room gets the accounting.*

**The text at Changi.** It said upgraded, and it said A380, which meant upstairs — nobody turns left on that aircraft, you climb. What the other rooms don't know is how long we sat with the phone between us on the lounge table, not saying anything, like the machine might change its mind if we celebrated. Twenty-one days later I can report the machine did not change its mind about us at any point.

**Gare du Nord.** Three men, one lanyard, one minute. The pré-plainte took four attachments and the French state received it with the warmth of a toll booth. But the record here shows what the paperwork doesn't: you were at my back the whole conversation, in two languages, and the tickets stayed where they were. The state got the attachments. I got the better evidence.

**The berth.** Let it be entered formally, in the one room where no mate can hear it: the berth was yours. Found by you, argued for by you, booked by you inside a day for a ship leaving in two. I have spent three weeks letting the story be told as our luck. It was your judgement. The teller loses the telling everywhere else; here the teller pays up.

✻ Off Stromboli the captain spent his forty free miles on a volcano because he liked the look of it, and the mountain did its own fireworks, and for one whole evening the weather vane stood still. No forecasts were consulted. You noticed, and had the grace to log it without comment until now.

**The agreed proportions.** Two glasses of wine and a pint, most nights, in the agreed proportions — the record having been corrected by the house after some early misreporting. The porthole did the talking. The cabin forgave the luggage. We argued about nothing at a professional standard and came in under budget on everything except gelato, which was never a controlled line.

**Tuesday, then Thursday.** At the table: crepi il lupo on the way in, faccia lei from then on, arrive hungry. On the plane: the bid is in, and if Qantas says no, we will still be upstairs in every way that counts. Saturday, the belt, the six of them, ordinary service resumes and the vessel returns to the command of its rightful officers.

Twenty-one days, and I would board again tomorrow — same berth, same company.

✻ Conditions remain grim. Between us that has always needed no translation.

glossary.def: Origin unknown. Ownership joint. Meaning: everything is wonderful. Delivered daily, without smiling, in either direction.
Statement of fact, entered in the record. Admissible. Not to be read aloud to the teller's mates.

glossary.term: Two glasses of wine and a pint.
glossary.def: The agreed proportions. The house apologises for the earlier reporting.
The answer to every question at any table in Sicily and, on reflection, at home.
May the wolf die. Deadpan. Deployed Tuesday, as rehearsed.
Stood still for one evening off Stromboli. Reinstated by breakfast, without discussion.

modes.programme:
LE DUMONT D'URVILLE — PROGRAMME DU JOUR
Any Saturday — Brisbane. Weather: unchecked, on principle.

07:00 — the crew of six resumes command of the vessel.
Mid-morning — the belt, as contracted.
Afternoon — ordinary service, performed to cruise standard.
Evening — two glasses of wine and a pint, in the agreed proportions.
Night — conditions remain grim.
